text: Nine minutes until the gate closes, and two ropes drop past Sora from the high doorway, uncoiling into the water.
Six Black Hound hunters slide down and splash in, weapons out: swords, a spear, a bow, a mage's staff, a shield.
Mok wades over to them, raises his cracked shield and draws his sword. He wants the core, and Jaeha's phone.
Jaeha points out that two minutes ago, Mok was holding him up.
And now he's putting Jaeha down, Mok says, the dead eyes back. Like he should have at Gate 0912.
The husks are spent, he tells his men. Kill the rat, and only Black Hound walks out.
Up in the doorway, Sora rests her chin on her crossbow. Don't mind her. She's only watching.
Then a red window: Operator overload. Only one summon can stay linked.
The light in Lyra's and Borro's eyes flickers like dying bulbs. Lyra wants to know why.
Jaeha has to choose. One link, one summon. And only one of them has ever held a wall alone.
He's sorry, he tells the other two. He can only hold one of them. Protect Yerin, and stay alive.
Their outlines vanish. Lyra and Borro drop into rest form, and a rest-form summon cannot fight.
So Nib steps out alone into the open water, knives reversed, facing seven hunters. Who's in charge here?
Jaeha gives the same answer as the night they met. I think... it's me. Hold the line, Nib.
Mok laughs. One husk against seven hunters? Cut it to pieces.
Nib once held a wall for nine days. He can hold seven men for nine minutes.
A grey memory: the Ninth Wall's battlement, and one small cloaked figure alone against a swarm.
Three hunters charge him at once, two swords and a spear.
Jaeha presses a hand to the water and closes his eyes. Everything that hits Nib, he'll carry.
Nib parries both swords and ducks the spear in a blur of sparks.
A blade slices across his arm. Nib doesn't flinch, and no blood comes.
Because the gash opens on Jaeha's arm instead. He doesn't make a sound.
Yerin presses her glowing hands to it, horrified. He's taking every cut! Then heal faster, says Lyra, notching an arrow anyway.
Nib kicks the spearman's legs out and drives a hilt into a swordsman's jaw.
An arrow hits him in the thigh.
Jaeha's thigh bleeds right where it struck. Carry at a hundred and forty percent, and he falls onto his hands.
Nib pulls the arrow out, snaps it in one hand, and keeps walking.
Up in the doorway, Sora leans forward. Her compass blazes, pointing straight at Nib.
A violet bolt from the mage's staff blasts Nib across the water.
A burn spreads down Jaeha's forearm, and he sags toward the water. Borro's huge hand catches him.
Borro can't fight in rest form. But he can still be a roof, and he covers Jaeha with his shell.
Smoking, Nib gets up and walks back into the middle of the seven.
This time Mok himself slashes, and catches Nib's cheek below the mask.
Under Borro's shell, a cut opens across Jaeha's cheek. His eyes never leave Nib.
Nib touches his cheek and finds no blood. Jaeha is the one bleeding again.
Jaeha smiles through it. That's his job. Nib's job is the line.
Five minutes forty until the gate closes.
And the amber in Nib's eye burns brighter, and brighter.
The hunters back away from the light pouring off him. Nib held the line for his Operator. Seal two of five becomes three.
Armour assembles out of the light: wall-blue plates edged in bronze, a pauldron with the nine-tower sigil, and his knives lengthen into a scout-captain's long knives.
In one turn, Nib cuts through both swordsmen's grips and belts. Their swords splash into the water.
A bronze bracer to the temple, and one of them folds into the water, out cold.
One leap cuts the archer's bowstring and the spear in half.
He pins the spearman under one bare foot, a knife at his throat, not touching it. Stay down.
The mage fires again. Nib cuts the bolt in half in mid-air.
He slices the staff into three pieces and catches its little core as it falls. The mage puts his hands up.
The shield-bearer charges. Nib vaults clean over him, and the man runs straight into a pile of rubble.
Six hunters, disarmed, and every single one alive. Only Mok is left standing.
Nib faces him across the water. You first.
Mok charges behind his cracked tower shield with a roar.
Nib meets him and drives both long knives, crossed, into the crack down its middle.
The shield splits in two, its hollow grip snaps, and Mok falls on his back in the water.
Nib holds a knife a finger's width from his throat: I won't kill you. But I'll hold you for him.
Four minutes ten.
Yerin and Lyra haul Jaeha out, bleeding from four wounds and grinning. The little one is terrifying, says Lyra. She wants armour too.
Then, from the snapped grip of Mok's shield, something wrapped in plastic and tape slides into the water.
For the first time, Mok looks terrified. Don't touch that!
Jaeha pulls free and crawls to it on his knees.
His shaking hands tear it open: an old phone in a cracked orange case, with a faded sticker of a stick figure in a vest, giving a thumbs-up.
The same stick figure Minseok doodled in the first pages of Jaeha's notebook.
Jaeha's eyes fill with tears. This is Minseok's phone.
Mok turns his face away. Nib asks it for everyone: why keep a dead man's phone in a shield for four years?
Up in the doorway, Sora steps back out of the torchlight, and she's gone.
After four years, the cracked screen flickers to life, its battery almost empty.
Han River. Four years ago. One video.
